issues.feedback: The spec mandates `git branch -f {base_branch} origin/{base_branch}` inside `sync_project_branch`, but this command fails if `{base_branch}` is checked out in any worktree (common daemon layout: main repo on base branch plus task worktree). This can make daemon dispatch fail. Define a worktree-safe update mechanism and add a test that reproduces this topology.

`maybe_create_project_branch()` is shared by daemon and interactive project creation. Unconditionally switching to `origin/{base_branch}` can break non-daemon repos without `origin/{base_branch}` and changes behavior for local-only base commits, which conflicts with the spec’s claim that interactive workflows are unaffected. Specify fallback/compatibility behavior explicitly.
Changing `sync_project_branch` signature requires updating more call sites than listed. `src/git/commit.rs:536` (test module) also calls it and must be updated, or compilation/tests will fail.

The spec says `DaemonRuntimeConfig` does not carry base-branch data, but it already includes `global_config` (which contains `git.base_branch`). Adding a separate `base_branch` field is likely redundant and can drift; either justify duplication or use existing config.

Test plan misses key risks: explicit assertion that parent-project branch resolution remains unchanged, behavior when `origin/{base_branch}` is missing/misconfigured, and a real daemon/worktree integration case proving new project branches track current remote HEAD in actual dispatch flow.
